note: Requirement-to-production-test matrix for the v0.8 deterministic gate. Rows are owned by the canonical wiki pages named in ISSUE-0008. A covered row names a test that executes in tests/run.sh before this matrix plus the assertion tokens and any assertion source that test drives; tests/tools/test-matrix.py requires every named script to run before the matrix, every named source to be driven by that script, and every token to be a distinctive expression on an asserting line. A partial, missing, device, live, human or explicit row names a located blocker and is never counted as a pass.

rows.requirement: GenerationContext bounds: the 8192 UTF-8 byte bound, the wire-kind set, inclusive schema depth 8 and 32 record fields, wire bounds, duplicate fields or keys and trailing JSON are rejected; accessors preserve frozen data.
rows.evidence: The packaged consumer rejects each bound and accepts depth 8 and 32 fields; test-admission-policy.py rechecks the single validator.
asserts: depth 8 is inside the schema depth bound
the caller's schema object is copied before it is stored
an accessor copies the data, not the whitespace

rows.requirement: Request single use and cancellation, run admission persist-before-activate, repeated and concurrent run, close/release/forget/saved/shutdown ordering.
rows.evidence: Frozen requests, cancellation, single-flight and live Session reuse, saved release rejection and closure/forget are asserted on the packaged controller.

rows.requirement: next with an issued cursor reads the current state and registers a wait for a later state or fault; waits coalesce under the configured per-Session bound, release their slot when answered or rejected, are counted per Session, are absent from the transport containment pool, and a closed Session rejects a plain read and a registered wait; published acknowledges only a produced version and refuses a later one; versions are monotone business revisions.
rows.evidence: The compiled controller admits two coalesced waits under its configured bound, refuses the third with LIMIT, counts waits per Session, frees a slot on a rejected or answered native next, refuses a later version, keeps waits out of the transport pool and rejects both a plain read and a registered wait after close; a broken controller wait policy fails this test. The cursor those waits are keyed by is validated by the adapter, which the `host-cursor-identity` row proves.
asserts: the configured bound admits both waits
a rejected wait releases its slot
a closed Session rejects a registered wait
an earlier reported version never lowers the Session version

rows.requirement: A Session cursor is accepted only by the Session that issued it and only at or below that Session's current revision: a tampered signature, a truncated or empty signature, another Session's cursor, a revision ahead of the current one, a negative or leading-zero revision, a missing or extra part and a cursor longer than any issued one each raise INVALID_CURSOR, while an issued cursor reads its own revision and stays valid while it is still current.
rows.evidence: The production validator android/src/UpdateCursor.kt that Embedding.nextAsync hands every nonempty cursor to - and the only code that parses a cursor - is compiled unchanged with the public failure type; it accepts an issued cursor at and below its revision and refuses every tampered, foreign, malformed, advanced and over-long value. No issued cursor is 85 characters or longer, so an over-long value is refused by its signature or by the declared length bound; the case pins that it is refused. The `cursor` seam probe removes the signature comparison and this test fails on the tampered-signature case.

rows.requirement: dispatch validates the issued slot and carries the string-or-null transport - a literal string, a JSON-number string, true/false, the empty string, null and a structured payload - to the mechanism unchanged; the shipped session decodes it by the issued action signature (booleans from true/false, numbers from JSON numbers, literal strings) and a rejected spelling dispatches nothing.
rows.evidence: The compiled controller admits a valid slot and transmits every payload kind unchanged; the shipped Deal UI session at tests/tools/test-emitted-runtime.js decodes the declared boolean and number payloads and refuses a bad boolean spelling. The decode itself runs in the pinned Deal UI session, not a second implementation here.
asserts: every payload kind crosses the transport unchanged
a string spelling of a boolean dispatches nothing

rows.requirement: requestTrace and sessionTrace are issued, opaque identities that equal the trace the controller handed the generation and store mechanisms, stay stable for their lifetime, reject an unissued or closed handle and a stopped embedding, and the returned value survives close.
rows.evidence: The trace handed to generate and the trace returned when the store started are the values the accessors return; unissued, closed and stopped handles are rejected while a returned trace is unchanged by close. Filtering retained events by that trace is store behaviour and is recorded by the observation-store row.
asserts: requestTrace is the trace generation received
sessionTrace is the trace the store issued

rows.requirement: events enforces the configured 1-200 limit domain, hands an issued continuation cursor and a supplied trace identity to the observation store, and reports the store incomplete flag; the recorded health snapshot and an artifact status with its text cross the compiled consumer.
rows.evidence: The limit domain, the continuation cursor, the trace identity, the health snapshot and the classified artifact status cross the compiled consumer; selecting by trace, appending and clearing the retained store, the stored artifact hash and the lost-event accounting are device concerns recorded by the observation-store row.
asserts: health reports the recorded observation snapshot
an unavailable artifact keeps its status and empty text
a trace-selected page is returned to the host

rows.requirement: The retained observation store selects events by trace (an empty trace selects all), appends without invalidating an issued continuation, keeps at most 16 single-use continuations and invalidates them on clear, reports the sha256 of the stored artifact bytes, a truncated artifact as truncated, and recording loss or an unusable logger as incomplete health.
rows.blocker: Trace selection, continuation lifetime, the hash, the truncation marker and health loss are written by android/src/Observation.kt and android/src/bindings/EmbeddingLog.kt, both of which require an android.content.Context (and a JavaScriptSandbox engine for the logger sink); no deterministic vector can construct either without an installed device, so this item is proven only by the opting-in device lane.

rows.requirement: The closed discovery answer shape {title, brief, supportingFactIds, capabilityIds} with its title, brief and reference bounds; abstention is null, overflow rejects and never truncates.
rows.evidence: The compiled discovery policy rejects every closed-shape violation and accepts the inclusive title 120 and brief 4096 bounds; the `discovery` seam probe lowers the brief bound to 4095 and this test fails.
asserts: sixteen distinct fact references survive whole
sixteen distinct capability references survive whole

rows.requirement: The compiled intent is nonblank, at most 4096 UTF-16 units and is never the brief or its text; the prompt carries the disclosed facts and catalogue as data; re-admission returns for an issued suggestion with unchanged facts and catalogue and rejects with STALE for a superseded suggestion, changed facts or a changed catalogue.
rows.evidence: test-discovery.js asserts the compiled intent bounds, that the intent is neither the brief nor its text, the disclosed facts and catalogue in the prompt, and the STALE re-admission of a superseded suggestion, changed facts and changed catalogue. The request that handoff becomes is asserted by tests/tools/test-discovery-handoff.js.
asserts: assert(!intent.includes('Provide editable amount initialized to 84 EUR'))

rows.requirement: Acceptance of an issued suggestion issues exactly one Request whose title is the suggestion title and whose context carries the captured facts with the supporting fact and capability ids, granting no permission and invoking no provider.
rows.evidence: The handoff is compiled policy: core/discovery-policy.deal `handoff` returns the request title, the compiled intent, the three-field WireType schema and the captured-facts context bound to the suggestion's issued references, and android/src/discovery/Discovery.kt transports that plan through the one context validator and issues one Request. test-discovery-handoff.js drives the production compiled discovery bundle and the production compiled application consumer with only the native transport mocked: it asserts the plan's title/intent/schema/context, that an unissued fact or capability reference is refused, that the accepted context keeps its exact bytes and is consumed by exactly one `generate`, that no grant is issued and no provider or catalogue operation crosses the native boundary, and that the one context validator refuses a handoff context past the byte bound. It also reads android/src/discovery/Discovery.kt and pins the adapter to the compiled plan, one context validation and exactly one `api.request` call, because the adapter itself is Android-only.
asserts: 'the request title is the suggestion title'
'the request intent is the compiled intent'

rows.requirement: The migrated assistance view dispatches Open/Dismiss reducers and runs both host effects through the shipped session runtime.
rows.evidence: The compiled assistance bundle drives its real reducers and effects with only the transport stubbed; the seam probe renames the title state and this test fails.
asserts: Open sets busy through its reducer

rows.requirement: Compiled Open/Dismiss lifecycle: revalidate facts and catalogue, reuse a saved link before inference, one request, activation before saved link, retained dismissal, BUSY/DISABLED/STALE and no silent retry.
rows.evidence: core/assistance-policy.deal compiles the Open, saved-reuse, revalidation, activation-ordering, Dismiss-retention and failure decisions; android/src/discovery/AssistanceController.kt supplies the approved facts, enablement, retained dismissal and saved links and executes the transport. test-assistance-lifecycle.js drives the production compiled bundle with only the mechanism stubbed and asserts the decision for each case: one generate action per Open, BUSY for a duplicate, saved reuse with zero discovery and zero generation, STALE for changed facts and for activation after a fact change (no link recorded), mechanism-retained dismissal suppression, DISABLED without a failed attempt, no silent resume retry after a failure, and an explicit retry starting one new attempt. The refreshed catalogue is revalidated by the compiled handoff admission the Open path consumes, and test-discovery.js proves a changed catalogue rejects with STALE. The adapter that executes these decisions (single request/generate per Open, activation before the saved link, dismissal persistence) is pinned structurally by tests/tools/test-admission-policy.py, which is wiring evidence rather than a behavioural proof.
asserts: 'the saved link is recorded after activation'
'Open reuses the saved link without a request'
'a second Open while an attempt is outstanding is BUSY'
'activation after a fact change is refused'
'a failed attempt is not rerun on resume'

rows.requirement: Every capability-contract bound of the spec table is rejected with a located INVALID_ARGUMENT and disclosure is atomic over the accepted set.
rows.evidence: Version, byte, function, parameter, module and description bounds are exercised; a rejected contract changes no accepted set or provider.
asserts: Admission must not invoke a provider

rows.requirement: A frozen screen/chat/card compile-input target is required and out-of-set or absent targets reject with ADMISSION_TARGET before activation.
rows.evidence: The compiled CompileInput target validator accepts exactly screen/chat/card and resolves an absent or out-of-set value to null; ingress admission rejects an out-of-set or absent target with ADMISSION_TARGET, and the composer path refuses an absent target with ADMISSION_TARGET before writing a manifest and records each issued target when it composes.
asserts: a rejected compile input writes no manifest

rows.requirement: The public generate/load/check/mount/edit/save/cold-restore path carries the private target and no promotion or legacy record mounts.
rows.blocker: Production generate/load/check/mount/edit/save/cold-restore target transport is exercised only by tests/android/TargetTransportChecks.kt on a serialized device. The deterministic lane proves the frozen compile-input target, accepts screen/chat/card through the composer fixture, and rejects print and absent targets with ADMISSION_TARGET in ingress admission (tests/tools/fixtures/RendererRulesTest.kt:284-285); the production manifest writer and the mounted transport remain device-only.

rows.requirement: Typed plan values: a number for amount, percent and count inputs, a string for text, a boolean for toggle, an integral count, an in-range choice index, and a value inside its declared min and max all decode; a wrong-typed value, a fractional count, an out-of-range choice index and a value outside its declared bounds each reject at the decode boundary.
rows.evidence: The real plan decoder is compiled and executed: it accepts an amount, a percent, a text, a toggle, a count, a choice index and a bounded amount declaring their own kinds and rejects the same inputs with a wrong kind, a fractional count, an out-of-range choice index and a value above its maximum or below its minimum.
asserts: Typed inputs decode with their declared kinds
Choice index outside its options admitted
Input above its declared maximum admitted
Input below its declared minimum admitted

rows.requirement: DEAL v1.6 typed collections keep their invariant element types and array identity, dynamic JSON arrays convert into the same UTF-16 units including an unpaired surrogate and astral pairs, and emitted source literals round-trip the tested astral, unpaired-surrogate, control, quote, backslash and newline spellings.
rows.evidence: The compiled decoder and source-literal helpers are exercised directly: a typed string array keeps its identity, a dynamic array converts to the same UTF-16 units and the emitted literal parses back to the original text.
asserts: Dynamic array conversion lost UTF-16 units

rows.requirement: Shared disclosure predicate: a row, seed or note is admitted only when its content occurs in the frozen request or a disclosed fact; a rejected row never yields a trimmed record list.
rows.evidence: Disclosure acceptance and invention rejection run through the production construction call site; rejection leaves the instance unfilled.
asserts: the one predicate refuses the fabricated cell with its location
the decoded row list reaches construction unchanged

rows.requirement: countdown.length resolves seconds inputs and minutes constants with checked millisecond conversion; unissued, money, percent, count and nonfinite sources reject.
rows.blocker: Duration resolution does not exist: core/plan.deal:52 accepts countdown.length as an identifier only, with no unit lookup, checked millisecond conversion or rejection of unissued, money, percent, count and nonfinite sources, and no construction contract drives a duration. The clock/entry part behaviours (start/pause boundaries, completion once, entry keys, timestamps, totals) also have no deterministic vector; owner plan-schemas-values-and-parts (ISSUE-0003).

rows.requirement: Clock parts start/pause/complete once and restore paused; entry parts add typed values with stable keys, timestamps, undo and totals.
rows.blocker: No emitted clock or entries part is exercised end to end; construction contracts assert the part alternative only, and no test drives add/remove/undo, timestamps or totals.

rows.requirement: Well-typed formula and written formula evaluate with DEAL precedence, unary minus and not, comparison and lazy choose, zero ties and the floor/ceil/sqrt/abs/round/min/max calls; unknown identifiers, assignment, indexing, unavailable calls and mismatched branches reject.
rows.evidence: Formula evaluation and located rejections run through compiled policy; the seam probe changes an operator and this test fails.
asserts: Round tie at a negative half
round below a tie is not a ceiling

rows.requirement: Boolean operands short-circuit and the written-formula call set includes pow.
rows.blocker: core/formula.deal parses and evaluates both boolean operands eagerly and its call set omits pow, so neither short-circuit evaluation nor the pow call exists in the compiled formula policy; owner plan-schemas-values-and-parts (ISSUE-0003).

rows.requirement: A figure with the shared decimals field issues spec numeric presentation (NumberText/ClockText), a yes_no figure publishes a boolean and a written-formula figure shows its written form.
rows.blocker: core/parts.deal still emits a figure as ui.Text label + number + unit; no ui.NumberText or ui.ClockText is issued, so typed numeric presentation at the figure site has no production path.

rows.requirement: One issued operation per binding with parameter order, exact contract argument types, source ownership, duplicate and draft rejection and no partial publication.
rows.evidence: Parameter order, incompatible types, unissued sources and duplicate identities are exercised; the seam probe loosens schema compatibility and this test fails.

rows.requirement: One Slot per need with reads, writes, trigger, provider flag and allowed kinds; connections resolve on exact nominal type with required-optional rules, alignment takes the first other exact-name and type publisher in screen order with required-missing publishers failing and empty optional fallbacks, and Layout stack or unique integral positions resolve instances, capacity and unknown references with no cycles.
rows.blocker: The exercised fixtures assemble empty slots and connections (tests/tools/fixtures/catalogue-contracts.deal:274), so slot tampering, layout position resolution, capacity and cycle rejection have no production-seam proof. One aligned publisher pair is proven: the catalogue mode binds the checklist's done/total fields to the list_summary reader through construction.connect (core/construction.deal:33-51,129) and tests/tools/test-emitted-runtime.js asserts the bound summary. Unproven or absent: choice among several screen-order candidates and the plan-reads filter (core/construction.deal:39-41 skips a matching publisher whose covers name nothing the covering need reads), the required-reader rejection itself (core/construction.deal:47 drops the instance and leaves its slot open instead of failing the run, and core/screen.deal:136 is unreachable in production because screens.decode has no production caller), and any consumer of a declared optional fallback (core/screen.deal:63-65 only decodes and validates it, and core/composer.deal:85-102 binds a reader getter only from composition.connections, so an unconnected optional reader takes no fallback); owner ownership-slots-operations-and-assembly (ISSUE-0003).

rows.requirement: Every filled slot output issues its publish_/ready_ pair with the declared type; unfilled outputs stay open and unready with signature-correct getters.
rows.blocker: No publish_/ready_ pair is emitted by core/composer.deal, so publication and readiness have no production path to prove.

rows.requirement: Ownership uses the user probability at the 0.2 threshold; one owner per authoritative field and one producer per derived field; composite transactions commit once.
rows.blocker: Ownership confidence is compiled but no deterministic test drives the 0.2 user-owned threshold, a second owner or a composite transaction; segment coverage is claimed by no row.

rows.requirement: A free-drawing or motion request is classified once before planning as whole, part or none; unusable classification defaults ordinary without error and list/calculator/chart/button-game requests stay ordinary.
rows.blocker: No preliminary whole/part/none classification exists; whole writing is entered only when no runnable ordinary result exists.

rows.requirement: A chat target retains the first five visible needs with their hidden dependencies, removes orphan dependents to a fixpoint, discloses every omission as missing, rejects a header or three-section custom draft, and wraps multiple fragments in labelled Tabs with a retained selection.
rows.blocker: Screen.target is decoded and carried as a host-frozen compile input (core/generation.deal; android/src/EmbeddingConfig.kt:12-19; android/src/bindings/ExperienceGenerator.kt:44), but core/screen.deal rejects a promotion and no chat projection, five-need cut, omission disclosure, compact draft bound, header/three-section rejection or Tabs wrapper exists to exercise; tests/tools/fixtures/construction-contracts.deal only reserves an explicitly issued chat target. Owner generation-recovery-and-source-editing (ISSUE-0005).

rows.requirement: A scene need snapshots its read inputs at start, settles once, never mutates a plan input from its frame reducer, and the frame-scene exploration accepts or rejects per the Surface script.
rows.blocker: The scene need type is accepted and the Surface script exists, but scene construction, snapshot, settle, restart and the static-Surface acceptance have no implementation.

rows.requirement: Two selection batches with the decision thresholds, forced/settled choices kept, empty-response retry, unusable second batch stops, and the events question settles a trigger or leaves it open.
rows.blocker: Both batches and their thresholds run, but the second-stage decision list has no events question and no trigger selection reads spec.on/spec.at.

rows.requirement: Three ordered alignment rounds with eligible candidates, ledger/reading/quick-log preference, once-per-kind, replacement preservation, required-reader rejection, scene/written-formula bypass and normal stop.
rows.blocker: Alignment exists only as checklist into list_summary; the rounds, preferences, replacement preservation and stop rule are absent.

rows.requirement: Thresholded human-question review at 0.6, two blocking questions, option/text exclusivity and bounds, one answered replan, no reopen, cancellation ends generation.
rows.blocker: The adapter, option resolution and one answered replan exist, but the review does not retain its winning probability and admission decision, and no deterministic item exercises the 0.6 admission boundary.

rows.requirement: Fill order options -> concurrent grounding/live -> content -> active bodies with one owner per parameter and conflict rejection.
rows.blocker: Content fill and the catalogue disclosure gate run, but active hole-body fill is absent and the one-owner-per-parameter conflict has no vector.

rows.requirement: Coverage judgment against assembled behaviour, stage budgets and escalation, attempts counted per candidate check including failures, stop on repeated misses with the least-missing draft.
rows.blocker: Stage budgets, exact repair, check accounting and repeated-miss stopping run; catalogue body counters and the nested caps are absent, and no assertion counts attempts on the repeated-miss or retained-least-missing paths.

rows.requirement: Concurrent missing-need lookup with cache by need and contract digest, an 8000-character bound, named-refusal scoping and no provider substitution.
rows.blocker: No lookup mechanism declaration or refusal cache exists in compiled policy.

rows.requirement: Catalogue body fill: one ask per instance, two repairs, revert to default, per-instance abandonment, 600-character bound, independent counters.
rows.blocker: Catalogue instances still construct empty holes and bodies; no ask, counter, revert or abandonment path exists.

rows.requirement: Production compile of the candidate, manifest admission before any isolated step, isolated startup render and the compiled checker's synthetic-input steps; the accepted second candidate reports two attempts, one for its failed first check and one for its accepted second; a source check diagnostic is carried to the custom-edit ask while an operational provider failure ends the route with its own code.
rows.evidence: The packaged generation entry compiles each candidate, admits its manifest before isolation, renders the isolated startup tree and answers every synthetic-input step the compiled checker issues; the accepted second candidate reports two attempts, one for its failed first check and one for its accepted second; the custom-edit ask carries the FIXTURE_CHECK diagnostic; and an operational provider failure ends the route with PROVIDER_HTTP. The `attempts` seam probe turns the attempt increment that charges each custom-writing candidate into a multiplication and this test fails on that attempt count.
asserts: assert.equal(isolatedStarts,1,'admission rejects before any isolated step')
assert.equal(r.diagnostics,'FIXTURE_CHECK: retain exact pair and revise label')

rows.requirement: A candidate manifest whose imports leave the permitted surface is rejected with a located ADMISSION_IMPORT after compilation and before any isolated step, while a manifest of checked standard modules and embedding/graphics, and one that imports a declared frozen provider module, are admitted.
rows.evidence: The composed manifest is compiled by the real composer and then injected with an unissued module; the production admission rejects it with ADMISSION_IMPORT, discards the candidate and isolates nothing. A permitted-only manifest and the provider mode manifest, which imports and declares host/probe, are admitted.
asserts: admission rejects before any isolated step
the composed manifest imports the declared provider module

rows.requirement: An admission rejection authorizes no source repair, and a host/storage call is permitted only in an effect position while any other application-store access rejects.
rows.blocker: core/construction.deal repairs the assembled candidate on any returned check diagnostic, so ADMISSION_IMPORT and ADMISSION_PACK also open a bounded assembled-edit ask (the admission test observes exactly that), and no classification of admission rejections exists. No admission rule inspects whether a host/storage call sits in an effect position, so the effect-bound allowance and its rejection have no production path.

rows.requirement: Candidate admission runs the shared prop/card validator on the initial tree and on every synthetic handler, frame and pointer tree before activation, rejecting with a located CHECK_PROP naming the component, the prop and the class, or CHECK_CARD naming the component and the count, and retaining the diagnostics without activating a degraded tree.
rows.blocker: Candidate admission never invokes the shared validator: android/src/rendering/IngressValidation.kt has exactly one production caller, android/src/rendering/DealRenderer.kt:312, at render time (tests/tools/fixtures/RendererRulesTest.kt:19 drives it directly), and no CHECK_PROP or CHECK_CARD producer exists in core/ or android/src (grep over *.deal, *.kt, *.js, *.py). core/isolated-check.deal proves pack identity and the Surface script only, so an invalid candidate tree is activated with no located predicate rejection and no deterministic or device item drives this boundary.

rows.requirement: The serialized Session runs the same shared validator on every candidate tree before business-state/tree commit, retains the prior state and tree and starts no effect on failure, faults the Session with PROP_FAULT or CARD_FAULT naming the component, the prop and the class, keeps the failed evidence, and includes ordered NumberField/Slider bounds, time/date domains and TextField length/pattern constraints.
rows.blocker: No precommit validation exists: android/src/rendering/DealRenderer.kt:310-316 validates inside the composable and only draws the previously accepted tree, so no Session fault is retained, no business state or effect is guarded and commit ordering is never exercised. android/src/rendering/IngressValidation.kt:32-39 has no caller before a Session transition commits, and tests/tools/fixtures/RendererRulesTest.kt:19 drives the validator directly instead of through the Session commit path.

rows.requirement: Revision- and digest-bound exact edits; nonempty, unique, disjoint searches; atomic apply all or none; rejection preserves source, revision and diagnostics.
rows.evidence: Atomicity, staleness, ambiguity, overlap, Unicode and CRLF spans run through compiled policy; the seam probe removes ambiguity rejection and this test fails.
asserts: expected four issued revisions: two bases and two accepted edits
the digest does not bind the accepted pair in key order

rows.requirement: Structural add/remove/replace/move with the six-catalogue-instance bound, publisher preservation, rebuild as a revision-bound edit and compile before commit.
rows.blocker: No structural edit path exists; source edits only patch an existing pair.

rows.requirement: Live refinement copies the latest authoritative state by stable identity and type into an effect-suppressed replacement store and replaces atomically or retains the old Session.
rows.blocker: No live refinement or effect-suppressed replacement store exists.

rows.requirement: Every prop-value constraint class is exercised at the shared validator: finite, nonnegative, positive, integral-index, chart and pose each accept an in-range value and reject an out-of-range one, and display-clamp accepts an over-range value without faulting, while the clamped display itself is painter evidence owned by renderer-painters.
rows.evidence: The production validator and its projected classes exercise each class; the seam probe weakens Progress.maximum and this test fails.

rows.requirement: A style outside its family resolves to the family's allowed fallback and is not an error, an empty Motion style takes its declared pop default, and an unknown icon, a Tile span outside 1-2 and a non-string accessibilityLabel each reject with the component and the prop.
rows.evidence: The shipped style families resolve an unknown Text style to the body family value, give Motion its declared empty-style default and the ingress validator rejects the closed icon set, the span domain and a mistyped accessibility label.

rows.requirement: An empty style stays empty and is not replaced by its family default, except Motion, whose empty style takes its declared pop default, and an unknown style resolves through the declared order of allowed default, then body, then first style (docs/spec-v0.8.md:655).
rows.blocker: Both style-order clauses are unimplemented in production: android/src/rendering/PropResolution.kt:133-137 returns one family fallback for an empty style and for any style outside the family, so resolve("Text","") is "body", resolve("Button","") is "primary" and no allowed-default-then-body-then-first-style order exists. tests/tools/fixtures/RendererRulesTest.kt:193 and :202 assert the implemented fallback and the Motion pop default; no vector proves an empty non-Motion style staying empty or the ordered fallback rungs, so both clauses stay open rather than covered.

rows.requirement: Each declared payload class reconstructs its nominal value - a string from TextField, a boolean from Toggle, a number from Tabs, a row eventValue from ListItem and Path, a Button value, the Surface frame delta and pointer and a null action payload - while an undeclared card frame event and a wrong-typed payload are rejected before dispatch.
rows.evidence: The shipped EventPayloads module reconstructs each declared payload class and refuses a bad boolean spelling, an undeclared card frame event and a rejected numeric spelling.

rows.requirement: Numeric presentation keeps the value, its unit and its fields separate: fixed decimals round half away from zero, automatic decimals render the shortest round-tripping decimal, minimumDigits pads without truncating, affixes are unchanged, and the numeric-component site rejects a decimals value outside -1 or integral 0-6 and a minimumDigits outside positive integral with the component and the prop.
rows.evidence: The shipped numeric presentation and prop validators exercise automatic and fixed decimals, padding, affixes and the numeric-component domain rejections; the seam probe changes the rounding mode and this test fails.

rows.requirement: The shared decimals domain is applied by the figure and entry-field decoders themselves: a figure's absent value defaults to -1, -1 and an integral 0-6 decode at both sites, and 7, -2 and 1.5 reject at each site at the plan decode.
rows.evidence: The real plan decoder (core/plan.deal decimals()) is compiled and executed: it defaults an absent figure decimals to -1, accepts -1 and 6 on a figure and on an entry field, and rejects 7, -2 and 1.5 at each of the two sites.

rows.requirement: A reading_status catalogue parameter that issues the shared decimals field keeps the same -1 auto or integral 0-6 domain and rejects -2, 7 and 1.5 with the instance identifier (docs/spec-v0.8.md:186,457).
rows.blocker: The reading_status parameter site does not exist: core/catalogue.deal defines 12 kinds and no reading_status definition, so its optional decimals parameter is never decoded and no vector can reject 7, -2 or 1.5 at that site. The owning kind is the missing row catalogue-reading_status.

rows.requirement: The card profile admits only its components, events, props and limits: five pictures of 60 shapes, five Motion, three native Timer; a violation faults with CARD_FAULT and nothing truncates.
rows.evidence: Card membership, picture shape counts, Motion/Timer limits, Path rotation and static Surface frame targeting are exercised by the shipped rule modules; the `card-limits` seam probe raises the projected native Timer limit to four and this test fails.

rows.requirement: Nominal shapes, pointer phases, variant fields, finite numbers, lineWidth, alpha, paired points and commands; the 4000-shape, depth-12 and 1000-point bounds are accepted and one past each faults without truncation.
rows.evidence: The shared graphics validator accepts the declared variants and faults each limit boundary.
asserts: a nonfinite shape field must be refused

rows.requirement: Actual Compose painting and resource lifetime for every declared component, prop, child, style and event, including Tabs child content, Timer ticks, images, transforms, chart modes, feedback and the card profile.
rows.blocker: Deterministic items prove rules, metadata and inventory; actual painter behaviour is exercised only by the opt-in device APK (ImageChecks, TabChecks, TimerPainterChecks, TargetTransportChecks) and human visual acceptance remains separate. The Progress and ProgressRing display clamp (android/src/rendering/DealRenderer.kt:558,561,566,568) needs an actual painter review in that lane.

rows.requirement: One renderer entry per pack component, unique capabilities, projection integrity, and the pack digest and version recorded in the admission manifest; a changed digest or version is rejected with ADMISSION_PACK.
rows.test: bash tests/tools/test-renderer-rules.sh python3 tests/tools/test-vocabulary.py node tests/tools/test-generation-cutover.js
rows.evidence: The renderer entry set, unique derived capabilities and the declaration projections are asserted against the packaged pack by RendererRulesTest; pack conformance and the manifest identity are asserted by test-vocabulary and the admission rejects a changed digest and a changed version with ADMISSION_PACK before any isolated step.

rows.requirement: Duplicate pending taps preserve sequence, phase and revision; a stale sequence, wrong phase, an expired prerequisite, a pending invocation whose captured permission epoch moved or a send the host no longer grants admits nothing; a settled or invalidated record is re-admitted as a new invocation under the live grant that captures the live epoch; a rejected effect returns accepted:false; completions are admitted in arrival order and a continuation chains only from an admitted result.
rows.blocker: The compiled policy implements and proves admission on the serialized lane against the live record and the host's live facts: duplicate pending taps, unready, an expired prerequisite, foreign-lifetime, a revision disagreement (retreat or a live revision this record did not observe), a pending invocation whose captured permission epoch moved and a module the host no longer grants reject with their own codes and start no call, correlation is captured, invocationCurrent compares the live revision, the live grant and the epoch this invocation captured, and an invalidated pending operation is retired to stale/unknown with its call closed while another operation keeps its call. A retained stale or untrusted record withholds only its own reply and its own continuation: an explicit retry is a new invocation under the caller's new call identity, admitted instant and expiry, which leaves the invalidated reply unauthorized and is itself current, so its own reply completes. The grant is a live fact rather than a comparison with the earlier invocation's capture, so a regrant lets the retry proceed instead of refusing it for the rest of the Session. It is reachable from production generation only for dependency-set issuance: core/scalar-read.deal issues the emitted operation dependency set through execution.dependencySet, while admission itself has no Session adapter caller yet. Still missing: no Session adapter or emitted operation consults this decision, so effect rejection with accepted:false, continuation chaining and arrival-ordered completion remain on the operations.deal model exercised by test-construction-contracts.py, and no emitted operation transports an admitted record to the lane.

A reply under a revoked grant established currentness
A reply under a moved epoch established currentness
A stale pending invocation established currentness

rows.requirement: ExecutionLimits is the one host-configured containment block: every bound is validated finite and positive before any work, a sandbox constructed from it takes its evaluation timeout and heap, input and transfer bounds, the provider call and the disclosure refresh take their terminal instant from it rather than an adapter literal, and an unconfigured host keeps the 5000 ms provider and discovery deadline the adapters used to hard-code.
rows.evidence: The production ExecutionLimits is compiled with its fixture on a JDK: the defaults are exactly the previous 5000 ms deadline, a host-supplied provider or discovery bound moves the admitted terminal instant, and a zero or negative provider, discovery, evaluation, heap, input or transfer bound rejects. The adapter call sites need Android, so they are asserted from production source: the provider call takes limits.providerDeadline(now), the disclosure refresh takes limits.discoveryDeadline(SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()) and its wait consumes that deadline, the embedding threads config.execution into both adapters so neither can fall back to its own block, no 5000 ms numeral survives in either adapter outside a comment, and the block has one declaration. A sandbox constructed with the block takes its bounds, because SandboxProgram reads every one of them from it. The four sandbox call sites that still construct a sandbox without the block are recorded in the provider-invocation blocker, so this row claims only that the host can configure the contained paths named here.
asserts: a provider call must take its terminal instant from the configured bound
the provider deadline must not be an adapter literal
an unconfigured host must keep the 5000 ms provider and discovery deadline
the bounds must be declared once, in ExecutionLimits.kt

rows.requirement: Every journey proves fresh generation, a recomputing edit with no provider read, an invalid draft that withdraws dependent results and recovery, typed cold-reopen equality and no replay; Departure, Food and Equipment also prove pending-as-stale and explicit stale refresh, while Budget performs no external read so those clauses are inapplicable to it.
rows.blocker: The typed assertions are implemented in tests/android/CutoverInstrumentation.kt: Budget withdraws and recovers the typed difference, Departure preserves and edits the start and the unloading and inspection buffers, proves the disclosed 16:00-17:00 collection window and proves that a 00:10 start keeps departure and inspection on the previous day instead of wrapping them onto the task day, Food proves a typed arrival before 18:30, Equipment proves the required items, shared stock by a typed availability/stock value on the value's own availability label and that an invalid hire budget withdraws the computed feasibility, and every journey counts provider calls. Every journey's invalid draft is a well-formed number the control has to refuse (a fractional or unsafe amount, a negative distance, a negative or fractional quantity, a negative budget), because a malformed payload refused before commit records no Session fault and no revision and is reported as an unproven expectation instead: a control that refuses every candidate that way blocks the expectation, and a candidate accepted as valid that leaves the dependent evidence current fails it. A changed argument or period may display its invalidated reply staled by the value's own labels or by a stale disclosure in the value's own section, while an invalid draft must leave no current dependent value at all. A required expectation the view publishes no typed evidence for (the collection window, the previous-day instant, the delivery arrival, the shared-stock value, the interpreted cable length, a pending-as-stale transition not observed in flight after four bounded attempts) reports the journey blocked instead of checked. Budget performs no external read, so it proves the zero-read clause instead of pending-as-stale; the other three journeys prove the stale transition and its explicit refresh. The lane that runs them needs an installed provider set, explicit inference opt-in and a serialized device, so it is not part of tests/run.sh.
